Placebo standard error with poorly-fitting placebos trimmed

Source: R/placebo_se_trimmed.R
placebo_se_trimmed.Rd

synthdid's placebo variance permutes the control units, treats the last one as if it were treated, re-estimates, and takes the spread of those estimates. In a large heterogeneous donor pool most controls look nothing like the treated unit, so many placebo draws are fitted badly and produce large spurious "effects". Those draws fatten the tails of the reference distribution and inflate the standard error.

Usage

placebo_se_trimmed(est, replications = 200L, trim_k = 5, return_draws = FALSE)

Arguments

est

A synthdid_estimate object.

replications

Number of placebo permutations.

trim_k

Keep placebos whose pre-period trend RMSE is at most trim_k times the treated unit's. Inf disables trimming.

return_draws

Also return the per-draw estimates. Consumes no extra randomness, so a run with and without it gives the same se.

Value

A list: se, n_kept, n_total, treated_rmse, placebo_rmse_median, and – when return_draws is TRUE – draws, a data frame of draw, att, rmse, keep and placebo_unit (the control that stood in for the treated unit).

Details

The symptom is measurable with in-time placebos, where the true effect is zero by construction: in large heterogeneous pools |t| comes out far more concentrated near zero than the |N(0, 1)| a calibrated interval implies, while small homogeneous pools show no such compression.

The fix follows the spirit of Abadie, Diamond and Hainmueller (2010): restrict the placebo reference distribution to units the estimator can actually fit, by discarding placebos whose pre-treatment fit is worse than trim_k times the treated unit's. A placebo that cannot be fitted says nothing about how variable a well-fitted unit is – it is evidence of a bad match, not of uncertainty.

This trims the inference distribution, not the donor pool. The counterfactual is still built from every donor, and the criterion is pre-treatment fit, evaluated without reference to any unit's estimated effect, so it cannot be used to select donors that produce a preferred estimate.

Fit is measured the way fit_sdid() measures it: RMSE of the treated- minus-synthetic gap after removing its pre-period mean, on the covariate-adjusted outcome (see adjusted_outcome()).

Relationship to synthdid

Each placebo is refitted exactly as synthdid:::placebo_se() refits it: synthdid_estimate() on the permuted panel, with the original fit's options and its unit weights renormalised over the placebo controls as the starting point. Because an sc_estimate() or did_estimate() stores its fixed weights and options on the estimate, this reproduces those estimators too. The draws consume the RNG exactly as synthdid does, so under the same seed trim_k = Inf returns synthdid's sqrt(vcov(est, method = "placebo")) to machine precision.

References

Abadie, A., Diamond, A. and Hainmueller, J. (2010). Synthetic Control Methods for Comparative Case Studies. Journal of the American Statistical Association 105(490), 493-505.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("california_prop99", package = "synthdid")
setup <- synthdid::panel.matrices(california_prop99)
est <- synthdid::synthdid_estimate(setup$Y, setup$N0, setup$T0)
set.seed(1)
placebo_se_trimmed(est, replications = 50, trim_k = 5)$se
#> [1] 11.11442
# }
